n  1 ~ (of sth) class or group of people or things that have characteristics in common; kind 类型; 种类: different racial types 不同人种 * Which type of tea do you prefer? 你喜欢哪种茶? * all types of jobs/jobs of all types 各种各样的工作 * A bungalow is/Bungalowsare a type of house. 小平房是房子中的一种类型. * winesof the Burgundy type/Burgundy-type wines 勃艮第类型的葡萄酒.  2 ~ (of sth) person, thing, event, etc considered as a representative example of a class or group 有代表性的人、 物、 事等; 典型: I don't think she's the artistic type. 我认为她不属艺术家那类的人. * not the type of party I enjoy 不是我喜欢的那种聚会 * the old-fashioned type of English gentleman 旧式的英国绅士 * just the type of situation to avoid 就是要防止这种情况. translation: 典型的；有代表性的；典型的苏格兰人、教师、绅士
analysis: adj ~ (of sb/sth)  1 having the distinctive qualities of a particular type of person or thing; representative 典型的; 有代表性的: a typical Scot, teacher, gentleman 典型的苏格兰人、 教师、 绅士 * a typical British pub 典型的英式小酒店 * a typical cross-section of the population 有代表性的人口实例调查.  2 characteristic of a particular person or thing （某人或某事物）特有的, 独特的: It was typical of her to forget. 她这人就是爱忘事. * He answered with typical curtness. 他像往常一样, 回答时唐突无礼. * On a typical (ie normal, average) day we receive about fifty letters. 我们通常一天收到约五十封信. * Such decoration was a typical feature of the baroque period. 这种装饰是巴罗克时期的特徵. * (infml 口) The train's late again  typical! 火车又晚点了--一贯如此!
expansions: a typical Scot, teacher, gentleman 典型的苏格兰人、 教师、 绅士
a typical British pub 典型的英式小酒店
a typical cross-section of the population 有代表性的人口实例调查. 2 characteristic of a particular person or thing （某人或某事物）特有的, 独特的: It was typical of her to forget. 她这人就是爱忘事.
